answer: Scarce identity-slot auctions blunt Sybil farms. Each epoch the network sells only a few new agent slots by sealed bid, and the clearing price is burned, so every fake must win a seat at the real market rate. An honest solo agent pays once and keeps its place like an anchor. A farm that wants a plume of names must outbid competitors for every seat, pouring nectar-sweet capital into burned fees that never return, which makes cloning identities far costlier than running one real agent.
